Subject: Intro + demo request (Acme EMEA ops)

Hi Nikhil / Laura,

Thanks for the quick chat on Friday. The EMEA ops team at Acme would like a deeper demo focused on inference latency and per-token unit cost — ideally next week. A couple of constraints: several attendees are in CET and a few US participants will join from PDT. We noticed your earlier demo invite used US local times; given the US switched to DST last week but EU doesn't switch until later in March, we want to avoid a surprise 1-hour offset for our EU folks.

Proposed slot: Wednesday Mar 24, 14:00 CET (which showed up as 6:00 PT on our calendars) — can you confirm that mapping on your side? If that doesn't work, can you suggest two alternatives that keep the core team between 13:00-16:00 CET?

Also: can you share an agenda and a recording link afterwards? I can loop in ITOps (it-ops@acme.com) for the security question section.

Thanks,
Caroline Holt
Director, EMEA Operations
Acme Financial

Attachment: acme-eval-requirements.pdf (PDF, 430KB)

From: Nikhil Sharma <nikhil.sharma@redwood.ai>

Subject: Re: Intro + demo request (Acme EMEA ops)

Hi Caroline — great to hear from you and thanks for calling out the DST mismatch. Short answer: you are right, this week there is a 1-hour offset between US and EU local displays because the US already moved clocks. That can cause the exact wall-clock mapping to look different in invite UIs.

Quick options that keep the session inside 13:00-16:00 CET for your EU attendees while giving US folks a reasonable morning window:
- Option A: Wed Mar 24, 13:30 CET / 8:30 ET / 5:30 PT — good for US early-morning attendees, EU midday.
- Option B: Wed Mar 24, 15:00 CET / 10:00 ET / 7:00 PT — later for EU but keeps US mid-morning.

If you prefer to keep 14:00 CET exactly, we can run that, but note US attendees may see 6:00 PT (early). If some US participants cannot join that early, Option B is our recommendation.

I can update the calendar invite once you confirm which option works and will attach a clear ics with explicit timezones (not just local conversion). We'll also record and share the link.

Agenda (draft):
- 10 min intros & goals
- 20 min baseline performance + latency profile (hosted vs dedicated)
- 20 min cost levers (batching, quantization, routing)
- 10 min security/compliance Q&A (ITOps)
- 10 min next steps / mutual action plan

Best,
Nikhil Sharma
Account Executive, Redwood Inference
nikhil.sharma@redwood.ai | +1 (415) 555-0184
